facts.fact: The World Bank diagnostic gives the mandate for birth registration and ownership of its data to the Ministry of Health, under the Registrar General of Births and Deaths, and says the government is taking over the eCRVS contract (no date given; document's published year used).

The World Bank diagnostic lists deployment of the eCRVS under World Bank lending operation P173287 ending August 2025, with WARDIP financing its cloud hosting and satellite connectivity and the Bank procuring registration-centre devices; it names no domestic budget line.

The World Bank diagnostic states that a National Digital ID and Digital Transformation Strategy for 2023-2028 was developed and put to a validation workshop on 16-17 May 2024, while listing the finalising of a National Digital ID and CRVS Strategy among its next steps.

The World Bank diagnostic dates the start of eCRVS mass registration to 2 August 2022 in the Greater Banjul Area, to move from manual to digital birth registration, with 1,167,460 people of all ages registered and issued birth certificates between August 2022 and February 2023.
The World Bank diagnostic states that the eCRVS birth module is in operation and a marriage module developed; it reports no death module in operation (no date given; document's published year used).

The World Bank diagnostic describes civil registration as a centralised system with a centralised register, carried out locally by Ministry of Health staff in each district at 258 health facilities and 79 centres, the civil registration offices holding digitalised registers; it does not say in terms that entry is online at the moment of registration (document's published year used).

The World Bank diagnostic counts 79 Civil Registration Offices as registration points with digitalised registers issuing birth certificates, with no total of offices against which to set it (document's published year used).

The World Bank diagnostic counts 258 health facility outlets where Ministry of Health staff carry out civil registration, described as mobile registration by health workers, alongside the 79 civil registration centres (document's published year used).

systems.country_label: electronic Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (eCRVS) system
systems.platform: HERA, vendor WCC; proprietary software with perpetual licence; cloud hosting on AWS financed by the World Bank
systems.owner: Ministry of Health, Registrar General of Births and Deaths
systems.tiers: centralised register; 258 health facilities and 79 civil registration offices; the document gives both August 2022 and 2023 for its introduction

systems.system: eCRVS mass registration campaign, August 2022 to February 2023
systems.tiers: began in the Greater Banjul Area; 1,167,460 individuals of all ages

systems.country_label: National ID Card; Gambia Biometric Identification System (GAMBIS)
systems.platform: Innovatrics from July 2009; Semlex from 1 October 2018 under a five-year PPP since expired
systems.owner: Ministry of Interior, Department of Immigration
systems.tiers: 6 fixed and 12 mobile enrolment centres; 831,747 card holders against 1.39 million adults

systems.system: integration of the eCRVS (HERA) with the electronic ID (eID) system, sharing one NIN
systems.owner: MoU between the Ministries of Health, Interior, and Communications and Digital Economy, March 2024
systems.tiers: user acceptance testing for health insurance cards completed April 2025; described as planned or under way

systems.system: eCRVS interoperability with the electronic Human Resource Management Information System and the electronic National Health Insurance System

systems.owner: financed by the World Bank under WARDIP

systems.tiers: stated as not linked with the foundational ID

note: Slide deck; birth registration coverage is given as 50% (1.2 million registered, per government), a share of people and not of offices. Geographic access is listed as a barrier, registration centres being few and distant.
